question: Can train-derived source-copy negatives move probability mass toward valid non-identity edits without materially harming de-novo generation in one direct causal-LM checkpoint?

model_contract.mode_expression: source=<EMPTY> versus a canonical source SMILES

training.initialization: continue the frozen P16 mixed LoRA adapter
training.capacity_note: pre-training CPU isolation left 173 eligible edit rows; fixed at 160 per mode before any model training
training.objective: chosen completion CE plus edit-only pairwise source-copy margin loss

validation.id_condition_definition: same condition family (active property names plus directions/around marker), disjoint exact row and nonempty source
validation.ood_definition: deterministically take all available strict condition-family-OOD rows first, then fill to 32 with exact-condition-OOD rows in known families; nonempty sources and targets remain training-isolated; report strict and fallback counts separately
validation.gate_view: ID-condition source-isolated only; OOD is diagnostic because strict family-OOD may be sparse

pilot_benchmark.status_label: pilot estimate; not full Table1 or full de-novo benchmark
pilot_benchmark.table1_subset: deterministic SHA256 rank, 2 rows per each of 10 moledit_task_key strata, total 20
pilot_benchmark.denovo_subset: deterministic SHA256 rank stratified 10 rows from 6-property and 10 rows from 7-property, total 20
pilot_benchmark.checkpoint_rule: P17 if expanded gate passes; otherwise the same frozen P17 checkpoint is evaluated once as a negative diagnostic
